knowledge:
- key_parameters: Method="library" in getTarget specifies that target information should be retrieved using the provided mass spectral library and target table ;; forceOpt=TRUE in optFrag forces the optimization of target fragments based on the background library ;; calibRI in getPeak is an optional retention index calibration function generated by getRI to adjust peak detection ;; plot=TRUE in getPeakScore generates a visual histogram of the similarity scores for the detected targets
- alternatives: The documentation notes that while many software tools exist for processing untargeted GC-MS data, SIMAT is specifically designed for GC-MS data acquired in SIM mode. Future versions plan to support mzML and mzXML formats alongside NIST MSL.
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing targeted GC-MS data acquired in selected ion monitoring (SIM) mode, or when planning a SIM experiment and needing to select optimal, non-overlapping fragments to monitor.
- pitfalls: Fragment optimization (optFrag) should ideally be performed before running the experiment, as optimizing fragments post-experiment is constrained by the specific fragments that were actually monitored during the run.

workflows.name: gc_sim_ms_analysis
workflows.intent: Process raw GC-SIM-MS data to identify target peaks, perform retention index calibration, and calculate similarity scores.
input: Run (list containing raw GC-SIM-MS run data, typically imported from a netCDF/CDF file)
target.table (list containing target compound names and fragment information)
Library (mass spectral library containing reference spectra)
RItable (data frame containing retention times and retention indices of standards)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the raw run data, target table, reference library, and RI standards ;; 2. Plot the Total Ion Chromatogram (TIC) ;; 3. Retrieve target information using getTarget ;; 4. Detect peaks in the run using getPeak ;; 5. Plot the Extracted Ion Chromatogram (EIC) for visual inspection ;; 6. Generate a retention index calibration function using getRI and re-detect peaks with RI adjustment ;; 7. Calculate and plot similarity scores using getPeakScore
workflows.code:
library(SIMAT)
data(Run)
data(target.table)
data(Library)
data(RItable)
plotTIC(Run = Run)
Targets <- getTarget(Method = "library", Library = Library, target.table = target.table)
runPeaks <- getPeak(Run = Run, Targets = Targets)
plotEIC(peakEIC = runPeaks[[1]][[1]])
calibRI <- getRI(RItable)
runPeaksRI <- getPeak(Run = Run, Targets = Targets, calibRI = calibRI)
Scores <- getPeakScore(runPeaks = runPeaks, plot = TRUE)

workflows.name: fragment_optimization
workflows.intent: Optimize the selection of target fragments using a background library to avoid overlapping peaks prior to conducting a SIM experiment.
input: target.table (list containing target compound names and initial fragment information)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the target table and background library ;; 2. Run the fragment optimization algorithm using optFrag to select the best fragments for the targets of interest
workflows.code:
library(SIMAT)
data(target.table)
data(Library)
optTargets <- optFrag(Library = Library, target.table = target.table, forceOpt = TRUE)
